headings.title: Competency of accused and spouse, cross-examination, and confidential communications
headings.reviewNote: Makes accused and spouse competent witnesses at their option without compulsion, subject to cross-examination on direct-examination matters and impeachment, while barring disclosure of confidential marital communications.

headings.title: Abrogation of spousal privilege in prosecutions involving child victims
headings.reviewNote: Makes spouse a competent witness against defendant spouse and abrogates all spousal privileges in chapter 565, 566, or 568 prosecutions involving an alleged victim under eighteen.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections, effective date 7-19-85, and 27 case annotations; optional accused/spousal testimony with confidential-communications bar and abrogation of spousal privilege in under-18 chapter 565/566/568 prosecutions verified.

headings.title: Video conference testimony by victim in civil trials involving domestic assault
headings.reviewNote: Permits a victim of a domestic assault offense under sections 565.072 to 565.076 to testify by video conference at a civil trial and requires circuit/associate judges to develop and post local rules and instructions online.

headings.title: Public telephone assistance for video conference appearances
headings.reviewNote: Requires circuit and associate circuit judges for each circuit to provide and post on the circuit court website a public telephone number for video-appearance assistance.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections and statutory history; permissive video-conference testimony by domestic assault victims in civil trials (sections 565.072 to 565.076), local rules, and posted public phone assistance verified.

headings.title: Definitions of crime stoppers organization and privileged communication
headings.reviewNote: Defines 'crime stoppers organization' and 'privileged communication' for purposes of this section.

headings.title: Privilege against disclosure or subpoena of crime stoppers communications
headings.reviewNote: Bars compelled testimony or subpoena production of privileged crime stoppers communications or related records in criminal proceedings or discovery.

headings.title: In camera inspection upon petition demonstrating favorable and relevant evidence
headings.reviewNote: Permits arrested or charged person to petition for in camera inspection of records of their own crime stoppers report upon alleging favorable, relevant evidence, allowing court-ordered disclosure if entitled.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 3 subsections and statutory history; crime stoppers definitions, criminal/discovery disclosure privilege, and defendant petition for in camera inspection verified.

headings.title: Execution by lethal gas or lethal injection and enclosed facility requirements
headings.reviewNote: Prescribes lethal gas or lethal injection as manner of death penalty execution and directs DOC director to provide an enclosed facility and necessary appliances.

headings.title: Selection and statutory confidentiality of execution team members
headings.reviewNote: Directs DOC director to select an execution team, makes member identities confidential and privileged from legal compulsion, and classifies lethal administration protocols as open and remaining protocols as closed.

headings.title: Civil cause of action for unauthorized disclosure of execution team identities
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits knowing unauthorized disclosure of current or former execution team identities or identifying records and creates a civil cause of action for actual damages and willful punitive damages.

headings.title: Licensing protections and state legal expense fund coverage for execution team
headings.reviewNote: Bars professional licensing discipline for lawful execution participation and provides section 105.711 state legal expense fund coverage (excluding chapter 287 claims).

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 4 subsections, statutory history, and 2 federal case annotations (Zink v. Lombardi, ACLU v. Lombardi); lethal gas/injection manner, execution team confidentiality/privilege, civil disclosure action, and licensing/legal expense fund protections verified.

headings.title: Hard labor and governance of persons committed to St. Louis City workhouse
headings.reviewNote: Requires persons committed to the St. Louis City workhouse or city prison by St. Louis circuit court to perform hard labor as health permits under municipal assembly rules.

headings.title: Per diem credit rate for fines and costs and six-month imprisonment cap
headings.reviewNote: Grants ten dollars per day work credit for committed persons unwilling though able to pay fines and costs, capping imprisonment for nonpayment at six months.

headings.title: Installment payments for fines and costs assessed by St. Louis circuit court
headings.reviewNote: Permits St. Louis City circuit court to provide for installment payment of assessed fines and costs on appropriate terms.

headings.title: Application for discharge upon full payment of fines and costs
headings.reviewNote: Directs open-court payment order, clerk receipt and execution satisfaction, written sealed notice to superintendent, and immediate discharge when a committed person applies to pay fine and costs.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 4 subsections, statutory history, and effective date 1-02-79; St. Louis City workhouse hard labor, $10/day credit with 6-month nonpayment cap, installment fines, and payment-discharge procedure verified.
